body.statement:
Let \(h_{\min}=\min_{i\le N}h_i\), which is positive under \(\texttt{ass:variance-replication}\), and define the oracle residual variance
\[
 \widetilde\sigma_i^2=h_i^{-1}\sum_{t\in H_i}e_{it}^2.
\]
There is a constant \(C_1<\infty\), depending only on \(C_e\) and \(\bar\sigma\), such that, for every \(x\ge0\),
\[
 \sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY}}}P_n\!\left\{
 \max_{i\le N}|\widetilde\sigma_i^2-\sigma_i^2|>
 C_1\left[\sqrt{\frac{\log(2N)+x}{h_{\min}}}
 +\frac{\log(2N)+x}{h_{\min}}\right]\right\}\le2e^{-x}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \max_{i\le N}|\widetilde\sigma_i^2-\sigma_i^2|
 =O_{P_n}\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log(2N)}{h_{\min}}}
 +\frac{\log(2N)}{h_{\min}}\right)
 =o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2})
\]
uniformly over the finite slices.  For
\[
 d_{it}=\widehat m_{it}^{0,(-it)}-m^0_{it},
 \qquad
 d_i^2=h_i^{-1}\sum_{t\in H_i}d_{it}^2,
\]
the feasible residual variance has the exact contamination bound
\[
 |\widehat\sigma_i^2-\widetilde\sigma_i^2|
 \le2\left(h_i^{-1}\sum_{t\in H_i}e_{it}^2\right)^{1/2}d_i+d_i^2.
\]
Finally, set
\[
 \widehat b_{kq}=\widehat c_{kq}\widehat\sigma_u/s_k,
 \qquad
 r_n^{\mathrm{score}}=\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}
 \left\{\sum_{q=(u,v)\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}
 (\widehat b_{kq}-a_{kq})^2\right\}^{1/2},
\]
and \(\mathcal B_n(h)=\{r_n^{\mathrm{score}}\le h\}\).  On \(\mathcal B_n(h)\), with \(\delta_h=2h+h^2<1\),
\[
 \max_{k,k'\in\mathcal K_n}
 \frac{|\widehat\Omega_{kk'}-\Omega_{kk'}|}{s_ks_{k'}}\le\delta_h,
 \qquad
 \max_k\left|\frac{\widehat s_k}{s_k}-1\right|
 \le\frac{\delta_h}{1+\sqrt{1-\delta_h}},
\]
and
\[
 \|\widehat\Sigma_n-\Sigma_n\|_{\max}
 \le\frac{2\delta_h}{1-\delta_h}.
\]
These are deterministic consequences of the displayed score discrepancy.  No stochastic rate for \(r_n^{\mathrm{score}}\) is asserted.
body.justification: The theorem separates the variance component that replication identifies from the imputation and loading components that the frozen assumptions do not control.
body.gap: Available feasible low-rank central limit theorems concern fixed functionals and do not establish the growing normalized rowwise \(\ell_2\) score rate required by this plug-in covariance.
body.consumer: The deterministic map \(r_n^{\mathrm{score}}\mapsto(\widehat\Omega,\widehat s,\widehat\Sigma)\) is the feasible covariance input to the conditional multiplier comparison.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(h_{\min}=\min_{i\le N}h_i\).  The denominator in
\(\texttt{ass:variance-replication}\) is finite only when \(h_{\min}>0\), so
every oracle average in the statement is well defined.  By
\(\texttt{ass:row-heteroskedasticity}\),
\(E_{P_n}[e_{it}^2]=\sigma_i^2\) for \(t\in H_i\).  We first prove the
uniform concentration claim directly from the sub-Gaussian assumption.

The definition of the \(\psi_2\)-norm and
\(\|e_{it}\|_{\psi_2}\le C_e\sigma_i\) imply, after increasing a constant
depending only on \(C_e\), that
\[
 E_{P_n}\exp\{e_{it}^2/(C_2\sigma_i^2)\}\le2.
\]
For every integer \(m\ge1\), the elementary inequality
\(y^m\le m!e^y\) for \(y\ge0\) therefore gives
\[
 E_{P_n}|e_{it}|^{2m}\le2m!(C_2\sigma_i^2)^m.
\]
Let \(U_{it}=e_{it}^2-\sigma_i^2\).  Centeredness of \(U_{it}\), the last
display, \((x+y)^m\le2^{m-1}(x^m+y^m)\), and
\(\sigma_i\le\bar\sigma\) imply that, for every \(m\ge2\),
\[
 E_{P_n}|U_{it}|^m\le m!(C_3\bar\sigma^2)^m.
\]
Expanding the moment-generating function and using
\(E_{P_n}U_{it}=0\), for \(|\lambda|\le(2C_3\bar\sigma^2)^{-1}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_{P_n}e^{\lambda U_{it}}
 &=1+\sum_{m=2}^{\infty}\frac{\lambda^mE_{P_n}U_{it}^m}{m!}\\
 &\le1+\sum_{m=2}^{\infty}(|\lambda|C_3\bar\sigma^2)^m
 \le\exp(C_4\lambda^2\bar\sigma^4).
 \end{aligned}
\]
For fixed \(i\), the variables \(\{U_{it}:t\in H_i\}\) are independent by
\(\texttt{ass:independent-cells}\).  Multiplying their moment-generating
functions and optimizing the exponential Markov bound over the admissible
\(\lambda\) yields, for every \(y\ge0\),
\[
 P_n\!\left\{
 |\widetilde\sigma_i^2-\sigma_i^2|>
 C_5\bar\sigma^2\left(\sqrt{y/h_i}+y/h_i\right)
 \right\}\le2e^{-y}.
\]
Indeed, use \(\lambda\) proportional to
\(\min\{\sqrt{y/(h_i\bar\sigma^4)},1/\bar\sigma^2\}\) in the upper tail
and \(-\lambda\) in the lower tail.  Taking
\(y=\log(2N)+x\), using \(h_i\ge h_{\min}\), and applying Boole's inequality
over \(i\le N\) proves the first display in the statement after absorbing
\(\bar\sigma^2\) into \(C_1\).  Taking fixed large \(x\) proves the displayed
uniform \(O_{P_n}\) rate.

Put \(v_n=\sqrt{\log(2N)/h_{\min}}\).  Assumption
\(\texttt{ass:variance-replication}\) states
\[
 v_n\log^2(2K)\le\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm{vrep}}\longrightarrow0.
\]
It also implies \(v_n\to0\).  Hence
\[
 (v_n+v_n^2)\log^2(2K)
 \le\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm{vrep}}(1+v_n)\longrightarrow0,
\]
which proves the asserted \(o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2})\) oracle-variance rate.

For \(t\in H_i\), the observed cell is untreated, so the observation equation
gives \(Y_{it}=m^0_{it}+e_{it}\).  Therefore
\(\widehat e_{it}=e_{it}-d_{it}\), and exact expansion gives
\[
 \widehat\sigma_i^2-\widetilde\sigma_i^2
 =-\frac2{h_i}\sum_{t\in H_i}e_{it}d_{it}
   +\frac1{h_i}\sum_{t\in H_i}d_{it}^2.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz and the definition of \(d_i\) yield
\[
 \left|h_i^{-1}\sum_{t\in H_i}e_{it}d_{it}\right|
 \le\left(h_i^{-1}\sum_{t\in H_i}e_{it}^2\right)^{1/2}d_i.
\]
The contamination inequality follows by the triangle inequality.  Notice that
no frozen assumption bounds \(d_i\), so this exact inequality cannot be
promoted to a feasible variance rate.

We finally prove score stability.  By
\(\texttt{ass:row-heteroskedasticity}\), \(\sigma_{uv}=\sigma_u\).  The
definitions of \(a_{kq}\), \(s_k\), and \(\Omega_{kk}\), together with
\(s_k>0\) from \(\texttt{ass:horizon-variance-nondegeneracy}\), give
\[
 \|a_k\|_2^2=\sum_q a_{kq}^2
 =s_k^{-2}\sum_qc_{kq}^2\sigma_u^2
 =s_k^{-2}\Omega_{kk}=1.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \frac{\widehat\Omega_{kk'}}{s_ks_{k'}}
 =\sum_q\widehat b_{kq}\widehat b_{k'q},
 \qquad
 \frac{\Omega_{kk'}}{s_ks_{k'}}
 =\sum_qa_{kq}a_{k'q}.
\]
Writing \(u_k=\widehat b_k-a_k\), the difference of the two inner products is
\[
 \langle u_k,a_{k'}\rangle+\langle a_k,u_{k'}\rangle
 +\langle u_k,u_{k'}\rangle.
\]
On \(\mathcal B_n(h)\), Cauchy--Schwarz and \(\|a_k\|_2=1\) show that its
absolute value is at most \(h+h+h^2=\delta_h\), proving the covariance
inequality.

Set \(t_k=\widehat s_k/s_k\).  The diagonal case gives
\(|t_k^2-1|\le\delta_h\).  If \(\delta_h<1\), then
\(t_k\ge\sqrt{1-\delta_h}>0\), and
\[
 |t_k-1|=\frac{|t_k^2-1|}{t_k+1}
 \le\frac{\delta_h}{1+\sqrt{1-\delta_h}}.
\]
In particular, \(\widehat\Sigma_n\) is well defined.  Since
\(t_kt_{k'}\in[1-\delta_h,1+\delta_h]\), since
\(|\Sigma_{kk'}|\le1\) by Cauchy--Schwarz, and since the already proved
covariance discrepancy is at most \(\delta_h\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\widehat\Sigma_{kk'}-\Sigma_{kk'}|
 &\le\frac{\delta_h}{t_kt_{k'}}
 +|\Sigma_{kk'}|\left|\frac1{t_kt_{k'}}-1\right|\\
 &\le\frac{\delta_h}{1-\delta_h}
 +\frac{\delta_h}{1-\delta_h}
 =\frac{2\delta_h}{1-\delta_h}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This proves every claimed consequence while leaving the unprovided stochastic
score rate explicit.
